sketches.mechanism: Optional chaining returns nil and silently stops when any link in the chain is nil, rather than crashing
sketches.resonance: Reaching for someone through a chain of connections, only to have the whole attempt dissolve into nothing the moment one link is missing.

sketches.mechanism: Prolog's closed-world assumption: anything it cannot prove true is considered false
sketches.resonance: If love is never declared, the system concludes it does not exist — confusing silence with absence.

sketches.mechanism: The 'never' type represents values that can never occur; a function returning 'never' cannot return at all
sketches.resonance: A promise whose return type guarantees it will never be fulfilled — the type system itself forbids completion.
